{{nihongo|'''Tsuruichi Hayashi'''|林 鶴一|Hayashi Tsuruichi|extra=June 13, 1873 – October 4, 1935}} was a Japanese [[mathematician]] and [[historian]] of [[Japanese mathematics]]. He was born in [[Tokushima]], Japan.<ref>{{citation|last=Fujiwara|first=Matsusaburô|title=Obituary note, Tsuruichi Hayashi (1873–1935)|journal=[[Tohoku Mathematical Journal]]|volume=41|pages=265–289|date=1935–1936}}.</ref>

He was the founder of the ''[[Tohoku Mathematical Journal]]''.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Oda | first = Tadao
 | doi = 10.2748/tmj/1325886276
 | issue = 4
 | journal = [[Tohoku Mathematical Journal]]
 | mr = 2872951
 | pages = 461–470
 | series = Second Series
 | title = The first hundred years of the Tohoku mathematical journal
 | volume = 63
 | year = 2011| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>
